summary: Koyo Sakaino (1871–1933) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He founded Bukkyo Seito Doshikai and held posts at Toyo University (~1918–1933) and Komazawa University (~1924–1933).
Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. In 1995, Shimizu was attested as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

Koyu Tamura (1931–2022) specialized in Buddhist studies and Japanology, studying at the University of Tokyo between 1949 and 1989. His career included posts at Nishogakusha University and Toyo University (associate professor in 1972, professor emeritus 1977–2000).

Kozen Shaku (1849–1924) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Senmyō. He served as head priest at Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sange-ji (1882), taught at Nagano Prefectural Northern Chugakurin (1881), and founded Shakuson Shofukai (1893).

Kozui Otani (1876–1948) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied under Eun Maeda. He served as a fellow of the Royal Geographical Society (~1902) and 22nd Abbot of Nishi Hongan-ji (1903–1914).
Kripa Shankar Shukla (1918–2007) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He held posts at the University of Lucknow until 1959 and was attested there again in 1976.

Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya (1840–1932) was an Indology scholar who studied at Sanskrit College and Presidency University (graduating by 1860). He held posts at Presidency University (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).

Krishna Kanta Handiqui (1898–1982) was an Indologist educated at Calcutta, Oxford, Paris, and Berlin. He served as Principal of Jorhat College (1930–1948) and Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (1948–1957).

Krishna Mohan Banerjee (1813–1885) was an Indology, linguistics, and philosophy scholar who studied under Alexander Duff and at Bishop's College. He held teaching posts at Hare School (~1829–1831) and Bishop's College, Kolkata (Second Professor in 1852).

Krishna Venkateswara Sarma (1919–2005) worked in Indology and history/archaeology, studying under V. A. Ramaswami Sastri and at Kerala. He held key posts at Panjab University (1962–1980), Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, and Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1983–2005).

Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi (1918–2017) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Bangalore University and was attested in 1997 as Honorary Director at Dvaita Vedanta Studies and Upakulapati at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha.

Krishnanath Chatterjee is an Indology scholar who studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

Krishnaswamy Nachimuthu is an Indology and linguistics scholar. In 2021, he was attested with a post at École française d'Extrême-Orient and as an editorial board member for Studies on the History of Śaivism.

Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2018, she held posts as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

Kristin Scheible specializes in Buddhist and religious studies, having studied at Colby College and Harvard University under mentors including Anne E. Monius and Diana L. Eck. She held teaching posts at Harvard, Brown, and Bard College (attested 2008).

Kristina Myrvold is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Lund University (attested 2005–2008). In 2014, she was attested as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University.

Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) was a sinologist and religious studies scholar educated at EPHE and Paris Diderot. He held posts at EFEO (~1962–1973), EPHE (1972–2002), CNRS (1978–1985), Collège de France (1987–1992), and Fuzhou University (~2001–2021).

Krisztina Teleki (born 1978) specializes in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1997–2009), where she also served as a research fellow (~2009).
Kshanika Saha is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Nalinaksha Dutt and earned a PhD from the University of Calcutta (attested 1966).

Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ganganatha Jha. He held posts at the University of Allahabad (lecturer from 1924, professor in 1956) and directed the Research Institute at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
